title: Father's ultimatum and leaving home at eighteen
summary: His father threatened to put him out if he kept playing jazz; he moved to his cousin's house in North Pasadena and became a professional musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No, never got caught. Different things just kept up, and I kept slipping out, going to different places, and that's when he would suspicion and question me. And then we would have a set-to, and finally at the age of 18 he just put it to me bluntly, 'If you continue to do this, you'll have to leave my house.' So I told him, 'I think I will,' which he like to have fainted, but I didn't leave Pasadena. I stayed in Pasadena.
But you left home then at 18.
But moved out of the house. So that he said I was disgracing him by going out in this jazz business.

He couldn't stand that in any form. So I moved out to my cousin's house up in North Pasadena, and I was still going -- trying to go to school, which I did for a while, but finally had to quit, and from then on I was a professional musician.
